Subject: Data retention & purge — logs/backups/prompts (BrightMD)

Hi Tessa,

We are completing our supplier security review and need a concise statement and artifacts regarding Redwood Inference's data retention and deletion practices for a HIPAA-covered workload. Specifically:

- Primary question: What is the retention window for operational logs (access logs, request/response metadata) and backups that might contain PHI?
- Prompt data: Are prompts or user-provided text persisted beyond request time? If so, where and for how long? Is there an option to disable prompt retention entirely or enable an "ephemeral prompts" mode?
- Deletion proof: If a customer requests deletion for an account scope (all data tied to BrightMD account_id XYZ), what is the process and timeline? Will you provide an auditable certificate or export?
- Cross-border: Do backups or archived logs ever land in EU/other regions? We need assurances tied to SCCs/DPA clauses.

Can you provide a short formal statement we can present to our security/legal team plus any supporting artifacts (SOC 2, retention matrix, DPA excerpt) we can upload to our procurement platform?

We need this by EOD Tuesday (US PDT) to keep procurement on track.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
DPO, BrightMD

Hi Lena,

Thanks for the clear list — appreciate the urgency. Looping in Marcus (Security/Controls) for the technical specifics and Alex (your AE) for procurement coordination.

High-level answer here while Marcus prepares a formal artifact:
- Operational logs: default retention 90 days. Logs are write-once, encrypted at rest, and shrunk to metadata for longer-term telemetry.
- Backups: encrypted snapshots are retained for up to 365 days; some cross-region redundancy exists for DR — we can scope region residency under the DPA/SCCs.
- Prompts: by default we retain request logs and transient KV cache for up to 30 days for debugging and quality monitoring; customers can opt into an "ephemeral prompts" setting (no persistent storage of prompt or response content) at contract time.
- Deletion: account-level purge request triggers: (1) deletion of live customer data within 7 business days, (2) removal from active logs within 30 days, (3) backup snapshot purge window up to 365 days — we provide a deletion report and retention matrix.

Marcus — can you prepare a short formal statement (DPA-ready) plus the retention_matrix.xlsx and SOC2 artifact? Alex — I will send the HubSpot/DocuSign links and timeline in a follow-up.

Best,

Hi all,

See the attached retention_matrix.xlsx and redaction_playbook.pdf. Below is the formal technical statement you can use for procurement and the DPA annex. Feel free to paste into your intake.

--- Technical retention and deletion statement (Redwood Inference) ---
1) Operational logs (access logs, API request metadata, service metrics): retained by default for 90 days. Aggregated telemetry (no request text) may be retained longer for product analytics; this does not contain PHI.

2) Backups/snapshots: encrypted, stored in customer-specified region where possible. Standard retention 365 days for disaster recovery. Backups are immutable until their retention expiry; we support a backup-list purge process triggered by customer request with verification steps (see playbook).

3) Prompt/content retention: By default, request/response content is retained for up to 30 days to support debugging, quality monitoring, and model improvement workflows. For HIPAA-covered customers, we offer a contractual option: "No-Persist/Ephemeral Mode" which explicitly prevents persistent storage of prompt/response content (only ephemeral in-memory processing and short-lived KV caches).

4) Deletion process and evidence: On verified account deletion requests, Redwood will: (a) delete live artifacts within 7 business days; (b) remove entries from active logs within 30 calendar days; (c) schedule backup snapshot removals according to the backup retention policy (up to 365 days) with a targeted expedited purge option for enterprise customers under a separate SLA. After completion, Redwood will provide a deletion report (date/time, objects removed, operator id) and a signed confirmation PDF.

5) Cross-border and SCCs: Data residency is configurable per customer region. When cross-border transfer is necessary, Redwood relies on executed SCCs in our DPA and follows the transfer mechanisms applicable at the time of contract signing.

6) Audit artifacts available: SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), retention_matrix.xlsx (detailed mapping), redaction_playbook.pdf (steps for removal and verification), and a sample deletion confirmation template.

If BrightMD needs a shorter one-paragraph statement for procurement, use the first two bullets above and attach the SOC2 and retention matrix.

--- end statement ---

Attachments included: SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (redacted), retention_matrix.xlsx, redaction_playbook.pdf
